answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because opal only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, karst is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any ferrous approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
